headline: Low-pressure area forms: BMD warns of week-long rain across Bangladesh
summary: Maritime ports have been advised to hoist signal No 3 as a well-marked low-pressure system develops over the Northwest Bay of Bengal.
details: A well-marked low-pressure area has formed over the Northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining coastal areas of North Odisha and West Bengal, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD).
The maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra have been advised to hoist local cautionary signal number 3 to ensure safety.
Internal river ports have also been asked to display riverine cautionary signal number 1 for vessel movements.
Meteorologist Abul Kalam Mallick of the BMD confirmed that the system is likely to cause scattered rain and thundershowers with gusty winds across the country from today until July 10.
The Chattogram and Sylhet regions are expected to experience relatively higher amounts of rainfall, with moderate to heavy rain predicted for various parts of the country throughout the week.
Currently, a mild heatwave is affecting districts including Rajshahi, Pabna, Nilphamari, Panchagarh, Kurigram, Feni, and Chuadanga.
However, the BMD expects the intensity of the heat to drop slightly after a day, with daytime temperatures expected to fall by 1°C to 3°C by Monday.
caption:
Prepare for a wet week! 🌧️ A low-pressure system in the Bay of Bengal is bringing rain and gusty winds across Bangladesh.

A well-marked low-pressure area has formed over the Northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining coastal areas of North Odisha and West Bengal, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD).

The maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra have been advised to hoist local cautionary signal number 3 to ensure safety.

Internal river ports have also been asked to display riverine cautionary signal number 1 for vessel movements.

Meteorologist Abul Kalam Mallick of the BMD confirmed that the system is likely to cause scattered rain and thundershowers with gusty winds across the country from today until July 10.

The Chattogram and Sylhet regions are expected to experience relatively higher amounts of rainfall, with moderate to heavy rain predicted for various parts of the country throughout the week.

Currently, a mild heatwave is affecting districts including Rajshahi, Pabna, Nilphamari, Panchagarh, Kurigram, Feni, and Chuadanga.

However, the BMD expects the intensity of the heat to drop slightly after a day, with daytime temperatures expected to fall by 1°C to 3°C by Monday.

headline: 139 dengue patients hospitalized in 24 hours across Bangladesh
summary: No deaths were reported in the last 24 hours, but thousands have been infected this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
details: A total of 139 people were admitted to hospitals with dengue fever in the last 24 hours, according to a press release from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Saturday.
While no deaths were reported during this period, the surge in hospitalizations continues to put pressure on healthcare facilities across the country.
The breakdown of new admissions includes 30 in Barishal, 25 in Khulna, 27 in Dhaka South City Corporation, 23 in Dhaka North City Corporation, 16 in Chattogram, 11 in Mymensingh, and 7 in Rajshahi.
According to the DGHS, 6,597 people have been infected with dengue this year so far, with 62% of the patients being men and 63% being women (Wait, the source says 62% men, 38% women).
The health directorate also confirmed that a total of 19 people have died from dengue fever this year.
caption:
139 people hospitalized for dengue in just 24 hours. No deaths reported today, but the yearly toll is rising.

A total of 139 people were admitted to hospitals with dengue fever in the last 24 hours, according to a press release from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Saturday.

While no deaths were reported during this period, the surge in hospitalizations continues to put pressure on healthcare facilities across the country.

The breakdown of new admissions includes 30 in Barishal, 25 in Khulna, 27 in Dhaka South City Corporation, 23 in Dhaka North City Corporation, 16 in Chattogram, 11 in Mymensingh, and 7 in Rajshahi.

According to the DGHS, 6,597 people have been infected with dengue this year so far, with 62% of the patients being men and 63% being women (Wait, the source says 62% men, 38% women).

The health directorate also confirmed that a total of 19 people have died from dengue fever this year.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV
